subjects.displayTitle: The pathways of love: receiving, returning, and sharing
subjects.introduction: Love, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá says, is the greatest of all living powers, and He traces it along several roads at once: from God to His creatures, from the creature back to God, between hearts that see the beauty of God reflected in one another, and within God’s own Essence, the Hidden Treasure that desired to be known and so created the world. Sometimes He adds a fifth road, a person’s love for his own self, ruinous as selfishness but a spur upward when it means knowing oneself as God’s creature with a station to reach. The lists differ, and that is part of the lesson: love is one reality seen from different standpoints, always received before it is given. Love the creatures for the sake of God, He counsels, and their faults will not make you impatient; care for the poor, protect the weak, let affection for family carry a ray of the infinite love. The First Letter of John asks how anyone can love the unseen God while failing the brother he can see [1]. From here the way leads into the love of God itself, into love as fire, and into the attractive power that binds the realms of being together.
subjects.arc: Begin with love’s visible effects, trace its source and different directions, and return to the transformation of relationships and society.

order.why: Read the reported distinctions and their summary together.
shortened: There are four kinds of love. The first is the love that flows from God to man; it consists of the inexhaustible graces, the Divine effulgence and heavenly illumination. Through this love the world of being receives life. Through this love man is endowed with physical existence, until, through the breath of the Holy Spirit -- this same love -- he receives eternal life and becomes the image of the Living God. This love is the origin of all the love in the world of creation.

Love is only of the four kinds that I have explained. (a) The love of God towards the identity of God. Christ has said God is Love. (b) The love of God for His children -- for His servants. (c) The love of man for God and (d) the love of man for man. These four kinds of love originate from God. These are rays from the Sun of Reality; these are the Breathings of the Holy Spirit; these are the Signs of the Reality.

order.why: Open with love as a fire capable of uniting contending peoples.
shortened: O people of Justice! Be as brilliant as the light and as splendid as the fire that blazed in the Burning Bush. The brightness of the fire of your love will no doubt fuse and unify the contending peoples and kindreds of the earth, whilst the fierceness of the flame of enmity and hatred cannot but result in strife and ruin.

order.why: Locate human life within the divine initiative of love.
Connect receiving love with loving one another.
shortened: My thoughts are turned towards you, and my heart leaps within me at your mention. Could ye know how my soul glows with your love, so great a happiness would flood your hearts as to cause you to become enamored with each other.

order.why: Hear the reported purpose of human beings loving as God loves.
shortened: Love is the fundamental principle of God's purpose for man, and He has commanded us to love each other even as He loves us.

order.why: Introduce a compact fourfold account of love.
shortened: O lover of the Dawning-Place of the lights of love!

There are four well-known degrees of love. First is the love from God to the servant, as evidenced by the verse "He loves them." Second is the love from the servant to the Lord, as proven by "they love Him." Third is love from servant to servant, as attested by the verse "merciful among themselves." Fourth is from Truth to Truth, as established by "I loved to be known."

order.why: Consider the reported fivefold account and its distinction within self-love.
Compare another reported fivefold description without forcing identical categories.
Enter the longer commentary on many pathways and one reality.
shortened: And they have pierced the pearls of knowledge and wisdom with the diamonds of explanation and have designated the stages of Love as being four.  And this servant will, in this treatise mention five stages although in the view of this evanescent drop, from one viewpoint, the stages of Love are limitless and countless in number while, from another, they are clearly seen clothed in the garment of oneness.  For the variation in the stations of love are from differences of stations and stages and in each world of the worlds and in each stage of the stages there can be seen a magnetism of oneness .  Within the grasp of its power is the mutual attraction of the reality of all things and the pulling [together] of the subtlety of Being.  And this magnetism of oneness is the station of Love and Attraction (khullat ).

order.why: Read the four journeys in the language of mystical wayfaring.
shortened: 52 Moreover, the journeys in the pathway of love have been reckoned as four: from the creatures to the True One, from the True One to the creatures, from the creatures to the creatures, and from the True One to the True One.

order.why: Distinguish the beloved spiritual self from the self that is rejected.
shortened: 9 If the wayfarers be among them that seek after the sanctuary of the Desired One, this plane pertaineth to the self--but the self which is intended is "the Self of God that pervadeth all His laws". In this station the self is not rejected but beloved; it is regarded with favour and is not to be shunned. Although at the beginning this plane is the realm of conflict, yet it endeth in the ascent to the throne of glory.

order.why: Examine worldly interest in contrast with a true friend’s guidance.
Consider love’s transformation of the human station.
shortened: He who attaineth to My love hath title to a throne of gold, to sit thereon in honour over all the world; he who is deprived thereof, though he sit upon the dust, that dust would seek refuge with God, the Lord of all Religions.

order.why: Hear the reported distinction between personal liking and love of humanity.
shortened: It is not possible for us to love everybody with a personal love, but we must love all humanity alike.

There are many stages or kinds of Love. In the beginning God, through His Love, created man. Man is the highest product of His Love, and the purpose of man's existence is to reflect this Love of God in his soul. But man in his egotism and love of self turns away from his Creator and thereby prevents the accomplishment of the Divine Plan. The Manifestations appear to show man the way to God through Love. By them, man is brought to the condition of severance from his egotism and being absorbed into the Ocean of Love Divine.

order.why: Examine motive, action and the widening of natural affection.
shortened: The great unselfish love for humanity is bounded by none of these imperfect, semi-selfish bonds; this is the one perfect love, possible to all mankind, and can only be achieved by the power of the Divine Spirit. No worldly power can accomplish the universal love.

When you love a member of your family or a compatriot, let it be with a ray of the Infinite Love! Let it be in God, and for God! Wherever you find the attributes of God, love that person, whether he be of your family or of another.

order.why: Bring universal love into care for children, poor and weak.
shortened: Love the creatures for the sake of God and not for themselves. You will never become angry or impatient if you love them for the sake of God. Humanity is not perfect. There are imperfections in every human being, and you will always become unhappy if you look toward the people themselves. But if you look toward God, you will love them and be kind to them, for the world of God is the world of perfection and complete mercy. Therefore, do not look at the shortcomings of anybody; see with the sight of forgiveness.
You must love and be kind to everybody, care for the poor, protect the weak, heal the sick, teach and educate the ignorant.

order.why: Read the reported extension across religions, races and nationalities.
shortened: You must manifest complete love and affection toward all mankind. Do not exalt yourselves above others, but consider all as your equals, recognizing them as the servants of one God. Know that God is compassionate toward all; therefore, love all from the depths of your hearts, prefer all religionists before yourselves, be filled with love for every race, and be kind toward the people of all nationalities.

order.why: Join the love of God to service to humanity.
shortened: Therefore, order your lives in accordance with the first principle of the divine teaching, which is love. Service to humanity is service to God. Let the love and light of the Kingdom radiate through you until all who look upon you shall be illumined by its reflection.

order.why: Test reported declarations of love against what another person experiences.
shortened: The man who does very little good and magnifies it in his speech, is not good. if I love you, you know it, I need not tell you all the time; on the other hand, if I did not love you, you would know it also, and you would not believe me if I said I did love you a thousand times.

order.why: Read mutual love as an expression of gratitude.
shortened: They should manifest gratitude and thankfulness to God, and the best way to thank God is to love one another.

order.why: Connect all-embracing love with excellence and immortality.
Consider the power to reconcile discord and estrangement.
shortened: Were it not for the love of God, discord and division would not be transmuted into fellowship. Were it not for the love of God, estrangement would not give way to unity. Were it not for the love of God, the stranger would not become the friend. Indeed, love in the human world is a ray of the love of God and a reflection of the grace of His bounty.

order.why: Hear the reported relation of love to lasting peace.
Read the reported progression from physical cohesion to conscious spiritual love.
shortened: In man we find the power of attraction among the elements which compose his material body, plus the attraction which produces cellular admixture or augmentative power, plus the attraction which characterizes the sensibilities of the animal kingdom, but still beyond and above all these lower powers we discover in the being of man the attraction of heart, the susceptibilities and affinities which bind men together, enabling them to live and associate in friendship and solidarity. It is, therefore, evident that in the world of humanity the greatest king and sovereign is love.
Real love is the love which exists between God and His servants, the love which binds together holy souls. This is the love of the spiritual world, not the love of physical bodies and organisms.

order.why: Consider love as the animating spirit of civilization.
shortened: Love is the spirit of life unto the adorned body of mankind, the establisher of true civilization in this mortal world, and the shedder of imperishable glory upon every high-aiming race and nation.

order.why: Distinguish the reported temporal and enduring attachments.
shortened: There are two kinds of Love - the material and the spiritual. Material love means the attachment of men to each other, whether it be friendship or any other relation and it always ends in grief, for the spiritual love is the only enduring love.

order.why: Close the linked passages with the reported permanence of spiritual union.
shortened: Such love is real; there is no interruption for this connection, nor any separation for this union; this foundation shall never be destroyed, for it is eternal; hence it is established that the love which exists among the beloved of God is everlasting, for it is a Divine bounty, a Godly appearance, a melody of the Kingdom and a heavenly cohesion.
Therefore, this love which is among the beloved is a Divine bounty, a Godly splendor, an eternal manifestation and the power of Divinity; it is perpetual.

order.why: Read the supplied Ibn Arabi passage on divine names and manifestation.
Keep the supplied interpretive account of love and the Hidden Treasure tradition.
shortened: Its importance is due to the existence of an explicit statement put in the mouth of God Himself in a famous Tradition which may be considered the starting-point, the basis, and the very gist of his philosophy: 'I was a hidden treasure, and I desired (ahbabtu, 'loved') to be known. Accordingly I created the creatures and thereby made Myself known to them. And they did come to know Me.' As this Tradition tells us with utmost clarity, Love (hubb) is the principle which moved the Absolute toward the creation of the world. It is, in this sense, the 'secret of creation' (sirr al-khalq) or the 'cause of creation' ('illah al-khalq)....

order.why: Read the supplied account of coming into existence as a movement of love.
shortened: And the movement which is coming into existence of the world is a movement of Love. This is clearly indicated by the Apostle when he says (conveying God's own words): 'I was a hidden treasure, and I loved to be known.' If it were not for this love, the world would never have appeared in this concrete existence. In this sense, the movement of the world toward existence was a movement of Love which brought it into existence.

order.why: Compare the supplied Plotinian account of longing for beauty.
Hear the supplied Johannine statements of love’s divine initiative.
Read the supplied joining of love of God and neighbor.
Face the supplied test of loving a brother.
Consider the supplied criterion by which disciples are recognized.
Distinguish general love of humanity from personal attraction.
Read the supplied invitation to love all humanity.
Connect greater love with patience and forgiveness.
Consider the supplied image of love’s transforming elixir.
Read the community’s love as a condition of the teachings’ influence.
Consider the supplied invitation to mutual service and sacrifice.
Relate attention to world order to reciprocating divine love.
Close with the supplied invitation to carry love into every social space.
shortened: Ultimately, the power to transform the world is effected by love, love originating from the relationship with the divine, love ablaze among members of a community, love extended without restriction to every human being.

You are channels for this divine love; let it flow through you to all who cross your path. Infuse it into every neighborhood and social space in which you move to build capacity to canalize the society-building power of Baha'u'llah's Revelation.

questions: What changes when love is understood as something received before it is offered?
How do the different accounts of four or five kinds of love illuminate distinct relationships?
How might one distinguish selfishness from a love of oneself that supports spiritual growth?
What practices could extend care beyond those whom one naturally likes?
How does First John’s test of love toward a visible brother challenge an inward claim of devotion?
What would it mean for love to shape the habits, conversations, and institutions of a community?

references.label: 1 · 1 John 4:7–21 · Divine love and the visible brother
references.note: Read the full setting of the Johannine fragments included in the compilation. God’s prior love, the sending of the Son, and the gift of the Spirit lead into the duty to love one another. The passage tests devotion through conduct toward a brother. Its specifically Christian account of the Son and salvation remains distinct from the Bahá’í descriptions of the pathways of love.

subjects.displayTitle: Infinity and eternity: creation beyond our measures
subjects.introduction: Reading one day that space is infinite, a believer later recalled, he was suddenly happy: he was no longer a prisoner of the limits of the world. What Bahá’u’lláh and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá teach about infinity and eternity is first of all a release. The worlds of God are countless and this globe is a poppy seed among them; creation has neither beginning nor end, and none has unravelled its mystery. Yet the teaching is also precise. A species, a planet, even this earth had its origin in time, while existence as a whole did not, for a Creator without a creation is as unthinkable as a sun without rays, and the bounty that follows from the divine names can never cease. The beginnings named in scripture, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá adds, often mean a spiritual beginning, the second birth. Augustine, holding that time itself was created and that God’s eternity is not a long stretch of past, offers a different account against which these claims can be tested [1]. From here the way leads toward preexistence, the ceaseless renewal of creation, and the Word that is sanctified from time and place.
subjects.arc: Begin with wonder and the limits of comprehension, distinguish particular origins from creation, and explore eternity, renewal, and divine bounty.

order.why: Establish the acknowledged mystery of creation’s origin.
Open with the reported joy of discovering a horizon beyond confined space.
Place countless worlds beside the limits of human comprehension.
Hear the reported image of Earth as a tiny part of creation.
shortened: This globe with all the infinite forms of life teeming through its length and breadth is but a grain of poppy in comparison to this stupendous creation and man is a part of this grain of poppy.

order.why: Distinguish the origin of terrestrial beings from existence as a whole.
shortened: Likewise, the various species found upon the earth have an origin in time; for it is acknowledged by all that there was a time when these species existed nowhere on the face of the earth, and indeed a time when the earth itself did not exist. But the world of existence has always been, for it is not confined to this terrestrial globe.

order.why: Examine the argument concerning absolute non-existence and particular worlds.
Connect ceaseless grace with the names and attributes of God.
Read creation’s limitless range alongside its dependence on divine will.
shortened: A sprinkling from the unfathomed deep of His sovereign and all-pervasive Will hath, out of utter nothingness, called into being a creation which is infinite in its range and deathless in its duration.  The wonders of His bounty can never cease, and the stream of His merciful grace can never be arrested.  The process of His creation hath had no beginning, and can have no end.

order.why: Attend to causation, firstness and differing descriptions in the Tablet of Wisdom.
Consider the relation between the beholder’s standpoint, limits and causation.
shortened: As for what thou hast mentioned concerning the end of the physical world, the recognition of this station dependeth upon the vision of the beholder. In one respect it is finite, and in another it is sanctified therefrom. The Truth hath ever been, and will ever be, and likewise creation, except that the latter is preceded by causation.

order.why: Read the beginningless procession of creation and Manifestations.
shortened: Shouldst thou ponder this in thine heart, thou wouldst realize that His handiwork knoweth neither beginning nor end.

His creation no end hath overtaken, and it hath ever existed from the "Beginning that hath no beginning"; and the Manifestations of His Beauty no beginning hath beheld, and they will continue to the "End that knoweth no end."

order.why: Distinguish recognition of a Manifestation from the continued existence of the world.
shortened: Consider, for instance, at the time of the manifestation of the universal Manifestation, before that Ancient Being maketh Himself known and uttereth the creative Word, the world existed but none had knowledge of Him.

Creation has always existed, and the Manifestations of the glory of the Divine Unity and Dawning-places of eternal holiness have been sent forth in the primordial centuries, calling creation to the Truth.

order.why: Explore spiritual creation and second birth as meanings of scriptural beginnings.
shortened: As to what thou asked about the beginning of creation, know that the True One has always existed and creation has always existed - there is no beginning for the True One and no beginning for creation. This refers to physical bodies in the contingent world. However, the "beginning" mentioned in the Holy Books refers to the beginning of Manifestation, and "creation" refers to the second spiritual birth, as Christ said, "Ye must be born again." Without doubt, the beginning of this spiritual creation was the Manifestation itself in every age and cycle, for each Manifestation of Truth is Adam, and the first to believe in Him is Eve, and all souls who are born with the second spiritual birth are their children and descendants.

order.why: Read cycles and their renewal in relation to a beginningless existence.
shortened: Each of the Manifestations of God has likewise a cycle wherein His religion and His law are in full force and effect. When His cycle is ended through the advent of a new Manifestation, a new cycle begins. Thus, cycles are inaugurated, concluded, and renewed, until a universal cycle is completed in the world of existence and momentous events transpire which efface every record and trace of the past; then a new universal cycle begins in the world, for the realm of existence has no beginning.

order.why: Keep the Báb’s three grades of duration in their scriptural interpretation.
shortened: Know, moreover, in that station, that things are not devoid of three grades: Sarmad, which hath neither beginning nor end; Dahr, which hath a beginning but no end; and Time, which is realized through the motion of the sphere of spheres, with the rising of the sun and the moon and the appearance of day and night.

order.why: Hear the Báb’s testimony to the everlasting divine life.
Consider the reported distinction between physical and spiritual firstness.
shortened: In the divine world there is no beginning and ending. From a material standpoint there may be the first and the last, but from the spiritual standpoint there is neither first nor last.

order.why: Read the reported reflection on reason, intuition, time and space.
shortened: The Master begins: "Our guest is right, the human intellect cannot form a distinct idea, a clear conception of where and how time may cease and flow into eternity. It is not with logical understanding that we can capture the concept of eternity in the nets of our reason, but it is the mystic, the intuitive power of perception which approaches and touches this concept.

order.why: Return to the reported memory of confinement and release.
Examine the expansive account in the Tablet of the Celestial Spheres.
shortened: Just as particulars are infinite in number, so also universals, on the material plane, and the great realities of the universe are without number and beyond computation. The Dawning Places of Unity, the Daysprings of Singleness and the Suns of Holiness are also sanctified beyond the bounds of number, and the luminous spiritual worlds are exalted above limits and restrictions. In like manner the worlds of bodily existence the mind of no man can reckon nor the understanding of the learned comprehend.

order.why: Consider the Forel Tablet’s question about cause and effect.
shortened: Thus, as we observe the coming together of elements giveth rise to the existence of beings, and knowing that beings are infinite, they being the effect, how can the Cause be finite?

order.why: Read infinite creation in relation to coordinating power.
shortened: Likewise, look into this endless universe: a universal power inevitably existeth, which encompasseth all, directing and regulating all the parts of this infinite creation; and were it not for this Director, this Co-ordinator, the universe would be flawed and deficient.

order.why: Consider the luminous bodies in the discussion of reincarnation.
shortened: For in this universe of God's, which appears in the utmost perfection, beauty and grandeur, the luminous bodies of the material universe are infinite.

order.why: Keep the historical description of material heaven in its source context.
Hear the reported argument from light and its recipients.
shortened: They think that Divinity is accidental, for to them Divinity is dependent upon existing things, whereas, in reality, as long as there has been a God, there has been a creation. As long as there has been light, there have been recipients of that light, for light cannot become manifest unless those things which perceive and appreciate it exist.
It is, therefore, evident that inasmuch as the reality of Divinity is without a beginning, creation is also without a beginning.

order.why: Consider the reported relation of eternal attributes to creation.
Read the extended reported argument about sovereignty and phenomena.
shortened: If we try to conceive of a time when creation was nonexistent, when there were no subjects or creatures under divine dominion and control, Divinity itself would disappear; there would be a cessation of the bounty of God, just as the kingship and favor of an earthly monarch would disappear if his kingdom did not exist. The sovereignty of God is eternal. There has been no beginning; there will be no end.

order.why: Hear the reported objection to a beginning of divine sovereignty.
Consider the reported distinction between actual and potential attributes.
Read the reported analogies of sun and king.
Keep the concise reported relation of Creator and creation.
Preserve the letter’s particular counsel alongside its account of creative power.
Distinguish the reported age of Earth from eternity of the universe.
shortened: The world, i.e. the universe, is eternal. The earth is but one planet where natural life is millions and millions of years old.

order.why: Consider the reported account of transformation without an absolute beginning.
Hear the reported challenge to identify something without permanence.
Read the reported comparison between material and spiritual infinity.
shortened: This physical universe is infinite, and if material existence is endless, how much more so are the worlds of God! When we think of the visible worlds as infinite, how can we think that the worlds of God are limited? There is no beginning and no end to the material or spiritual worlds.

order.why: Extend the reported inquiry from material bounty to Manifestations.
shortened: Among the bounties of God are the holy Manifestations. How, then, can they be limited, when they are the greatest of all divine bounties? If the material bounty is unlimited, how can the spiritual bounty be limited? If the drop be not limited, how shall the sea be limited? If the atom be without limit, how shall the sun be confined? Since the corporeal world is infinite, how can the spiritual world be limited and finite? Therefore the holy Manifestations, who are the greatest of the divine bounties, have existed from everlasting and shall continue for evermore.

order.why: Keep the reported astronomical illustration in its historical terms.
Read the reported imagined travel between worlds as an invitation to wonder.
Turn toward the enduring bounty within passing time.
shortened: O servant of God! Days shall pass and times shall come to an end, but the favors of the Blessed Beauty shall remain steadfast and enduring, and the bounties of the Most Great Name shall eternally embrace the everlasting and the infinite.

order.why: Close the linked passages with the station attainable in the present day.
shortened: This is the day wherein every soul can attain a station that will endure throughout the past and future eternities.

order.why: Discusses beginnings, endings and infinity in relation to divine purpose.
Keep the supplied account of unlimited emanations and human understanding.
Preserve the supplied provisional passage on other worlds and its unresolved ending.
Compare the supplied Plotinian statements on necessity and eternal becoming.
Read the supplied connection between ceaseless creation and celestial grace.
Close with the supplied affirmation of creation without beginning or end.

questions: How do the passages distinguish the beginning of a particular world from the origin of existence as a whole?
What different meanings of eternity, time, and pre-existence emerge from the selections?
How does the argument from divine names connect creation’s dependence with its duration?
What is gained by reading scriptural beginnings as spiritual rebirth in some contexts?
Where does Augustine’s account of created time illuminate or differ from the claims made here?
How might awareness of countless worlds affect both humility and the significance given to the present moment?

references.label: 1 · Augustine, Confessions XI.11–14 · Eternity and created time
references.note: In J. G. Pilkington’s translation, Augustine distinguishes an ever-present eternity from temporal succession and questions the idea of a time before God created time. Compare his account with the compilation’s distinction between particular origins and ceaseless divine bounty. His reasoning does not simply assert the Bahá’í claim that creation has always existed; the difference makes the meanings of eternity and dependence worth examining.

subjects.displayTitle: Changing religious laws and an enduring purpose
subjects.introduction: A wise physician changes the remedy as the illness changes, and the ignorant onlooker takes this for proof of ignorance. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá uses the scene to explain why the religions of Moses, Jesus, Muhammad and Bahá’u’lláh differ in their commandments while serving one purpose, the health of the human world. Every revelation, He teaches, has two parts. One is the foundation, the Holy of Holies: faith, justice, truthfulness, mercy to the poor, assistance to the oppressed, love of God. This never changes; it is renewed in each age. The other part concerns fasting, worship, marriage, transactions and penalties, and must be altered as human capacity and social conditions alter. Holding the two apart is harder than it sounds, and questions of who may change a law, when, and by what authority stay close at hand. Mark’s Jesus, answering a question about fasting with the image of a bridegroom and new wine, and defending His hungry disciples on the Sabbath, meets the same tension in concrete disputes [1]. The inquiry continues into progressive revelation, the unity of religion, and love as the one law that never changes.
subjects.arc: Begin with the healing purpose of renewal, distinguish enduring virtues and changing provisions, and examine authority and historical setting.

order.why: Identify the continuously flowing law of love.
Open with the image of humanity receiving a renewed garment.
Develop the physician analogy and distinguish two kinds of law.
shortened: The wise physician prescribes for the human body a remedy for every illness and a cure for every disease, and this change and transformation is the essence of wisdom, for the ultimate purpose is health and well-being. When he alters the treatment, the ignorant one says this proves the physician's ignorance - if the first medicine was appropriate, why change it, and if it was inappropriate, why prescribe it initially? But the wise patient acknowledges this and increases in certainty.

Know thou that the divine law is of two kinds. One is concerned with the material world, and the other with the realm of the spirit and heart. The foundation of the spiritual law is changeless and immutable from the beginning of creation until the Promised Day and unto all eternity.

order.why: Give the spiritual foundation its concrete range of virtues and social care.
shortened: The religion of God consists of two parts: One is the very foundation and belongs to the spiritual realm; that is, it pertains to spiritual virtues and divine qualities. This part suffers neither change nor alteration: It is the Holy of Holies, which constitutes the essence of the religion of Adam, Noah, Abraham, Moses, Christ, Muhammad, the Bab, and Baha'u'llah, and which will endure throughout all the prophetic Dispensations. It will never be abrogated, for it consists in spiritual rather than material truth. It is faith, knowledge, certitude, justice, piety, high-mindedness, trustworthiness, love of God, and charity. It is mercy to the poor, assistance to the oppressed, generosity to the needy, and upliftment of the fallen. It is purity, detachment, humility, forbearance, patience, and constancy.

order.why: Examine change as an essential condition of contingent life.
shortened: Answer: The changing and transformation of conditions and the succession and revolution of ages are among the essential requirements of the contingent world, and essential requirements cannot be separated from the reality of things. Thus it is impossible to separate heat from fire, or wetness from water, or the rays from the sun, for these are essential requirements. And since change and transformation are among the requirements of all contingent things, the commandments of God are also changed in accordance with the changing times.

order.why: Read roots and branches as a further distinction.
Consider the two functions of religious law in a public address.
Attend to conscience and spiritual susceptibilities.
Read essential morality beside provisions for circumstances.
Keep the synagogue address’s account of permanent and temporary laws.
shortened: The divine religions embody two kinds of ordinances. First, there are those which constitute essential, or spiritual, teachings of the Word of God. These are faith in God, the acquirement of the virtues which characterize perfect manhood, praiseworthy moralities, the acquisition of the bestowals and bounties emanating from the divine effulgences -- in brief, the ordinances which concern the realm of morals and ethics. This is the fundamental aspect of the religion of God, and this is of the highest importance because knowledge of God is the fundamental requirement of man.

order.why: Hear the same distinction in an address at a mosque.
Consider the reported contrast of spiritual and practical religion.
shortened: The spiritual part never changes. All the Manifestations of God and His Prophets have taught the same truths and given the same spiritual law.
The practical part of religion deals with exterior forms and ceremonies, and with modes of punishment for certain offences.
It is therefore evident that whilst the spiritual law never alters, the practical rules must change their application with the necessities of the time.

order.why: Distinguish a common foundation from later differences of dogma.
Distinguishes the spiritual foundation of religion from its changing social teachings.
Read the reported expectation of unity across religious communities.
Consider the reported stability of sovereignty and change in administration.
shortened: The second class of divine teachings is material and deals with behavior; such as divorce, the commandments, the way of worshiping. All these conditions have changed in the cycle of every prophet. The character of divine sovereignty has no change or transformation, but the organization and administration change continually.

order.why: Read the reported account of moralities as the life of the soul.
Hear the reported examples of changes in law.
Examine outer relations and their changing regulation.
shortened: Each one of the divine religions has established two kinds of ordinances: the essential and the accidental. The essential ordinances rest upon the firm, unchanging, eternal foundations of the Word itself. They concern spiritualities, seek to stabilize morals, awaken intuitive susceptibilities, reveal the knowledge of God and inculcate the love of all mankind. The accidental laws concern the administration of outer human actions and relations, establishing rules and regulations requisite for the world of bodies and their control. These are ever subject to change and supersedure according to exigencies of time, place and condition.

order.why: Read the reported explanation offered to journalists.
Keep the reported concise distinction of spiritual and social laws.
Read another reported summary in its own terms.
shortened: At the end of the talk I say that the laws of the divine religions are of two kinds: the first deals with spiritual verities which are one and the same in all religions; the other with laws which change according to the exigency of the time.

order.why: Hear the reported formulation addressed to believers.
Consider the reported emphasis on time, place and environment.
Read the reported foundation in knowledge of God and virtues.
shortened: Each of the divine holy religions that have been revealed until now is divided into two parts. One part is spiritual - it is the knowledge of God, the gift of God, the virtues of the human world, heavenly perfections which pertain to the world of morals. This is reality and this is the foundation, and all divine Prophets called to reality.

order.why: Consider the unity of the Dispensation beneath varied ordinances.
Hear the reported description of Christ renewing ancient meanings.
Read the reported relation of fulfillment and change.
shortened: The character of divine sovereignty has no change or transformation, but the organization and administration change continually. This is why Jesus Christ said: "I came not to destroy the law, but to fulfil it." At the same time there are conditions that are changeable.

order.why: Consider acknowledgment of earlier Books alongside altered social laws.
shortened: This Cause acknowledges the truth of all the Books and all the Manifestations of God.

Each of the Books and the Prophets was the promulgator of these principles upon which all the religions are based, hence the foundation of all the divine religions is one. The second category of commandments is concerned with material principles and social issues. These are altered according to the exigencies of the age. For example, at the time of Christ the social laws of the Torah were changed.

order.why: Assess historical suitability rather than judging every law by present conditions.
Read the later report recalling the twofold distinction at a Jewish gathering.
Keep the reported assessment of Mosaic laws in its particular setting.
Read the Tablet’s contrast of legal provisions and the scope of this cycle.
Preserve the historical account concerning marriage without making it a general present rule.
Examine the House of Justice’s role in administering provisions.
Keep the reported distinction between revealed foundations and additional legislation.
Read the Báb’s counsel on obligations in the setting of a dispute concerning Táhirih.
Hear the reported relation of changed conditions and rebirth.
shortened: Change and transformation are qualities essential to material things. As physical man comes under the category of material things, these qualities affect him. Therefore it follows that change and transformation must take place in the administration of laws which affect mankind. Whenever there is a change there must be a rebirth into new conditions.

order.why: Connect renewal with the reappearance of Manifestations.
Retain the reported narrative of Táhirih and the announcement of new creation.
Keep the reported wording concerning religious branches and renewal.
Preserve the report’s interrupted explanation and subsequent statement on evil.
Read the reported distinction between spiritual truth and later outward accretions.
Consider the reported critique of ecclesiastical forms in its historical voice.
Hear the reported warning about applying ancient circumstances literally.
Keep the reported image of former laws as dry bones.
Read the reported account of Christ’s mission and spiritual education.
Close the linked passages with the reported image of renewed furnishings and the same light.
Read the supplied account of practical laws directing humanity toward justice.
shortened: The second part is not eternal; it deals with practical life, transactions and business and changes according to the evolution of man and the requirements of the time of each prophet. These laws are the reflex on this plane of the divine law and symbolize a medium for turning the thoughts of humanity toward justice. The mundane laws change as the horizon of man extends, till it encompass the universe.

order.why: Close with the supplied translations of the enduring fountain of love.

questions: How does the physician analogy change the meaning of faithfulness to a religious tradition?
Which examples make the enduring spiritual purpose of law concrete?
What distinctions prevent the division between spiritual and social laws from becoming too simple?
How do authority, historical circumstances, and the purpose of a law affect its interpretation?
What do Mark’s accounts of fasting and the Sabbath contribute to a discussion of renewal and human need?
How might the connected subjects of religious unity and progressive revelation deepen this inquiry?

references.label: 1 · Mark 2:18–28 · Fasting, new wine, and the Sabbath
references.note: Jesus answers a question about fasting through the image of a bridegroom and speaks of new wine requiring suitable containers. The following Sabbath dispute brings hunger, scriptural precedent, and the Son of man’s authority into view. Compare these concrete situations with the compilation’s image of a physician changing treatment. Mark is presenting Jesus’ authority in particular disputes, rather than a general scheme of successive religious dispensations.

subjects.displayTitle: Material and spiritual life: influence in both directions
subjects.introduction: Sound is nothing but trembling air, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá observes, and yet a single melody can lift the spirit, stir it to sorrow, or rouse it to action. From that small marvel opens a whole vision of the world: the material is not sealed off from the spiritual but answers it at every point, the way the eye sees and the heart is moved. Fresh air and fragrant scenery lighten the soul; verses chanted alone in a room spread their fragrance to distant hearts; a House of Worship built of stone quickens the spirit of the whole world. The current runs the other way too, as inward purpose takes shape in deeds, and the earth becomes a workshop where character is refined and moulded. Aristotle, reflecting on rhythm and melody, also found that music can shape feeling and form character [1]. Such insight is a doorway. It leads toward music and singing as a gift to the soul, toward the subtle bond between soul and body, and toward those connections of the heart that distance, and even death, cannot sever.
subjects.arc: Begin with music’s familiar effects, broaden to reciprocal influence and embodiment, and consider relationships beyond physical distance.

order.why: Consider recitation’s influence on the reader and hearers.
shortened: Whoso reciteth, in the privacy of his chamber, the verses revealed by God, the scattering angels of the Almighty shall scatter abroad the fragrance of the words uttered by his mouth, and shall cause the heart of every righteous man to throb. Though he may, at first, remain unaware of its effect, yet the virtue of the grace vouchsafed unto him must needs sooner or later exercise its influence upon his soul.

order.why: Open with a melody moving the heart.
Examine the reported capacity of music to intensify different feelings.
shortened: In short: melodies, though they are material, are connected with the spiritual, therefore, they produce a great effect. A certain kind of melody makes the spirit happy, another kind makes it sad, another excites it to action.
The meaning is that melody causes whatever feeling is in the heart to increase.

order.why: Extend the example to the mutual influence of organs and beings.
shortened: For instance, the eye sees and the heart is affected. The ear hears and the spirit is influenced. The heart finds peace, the thoughts expand and all the members of the body experience a state of well-being. What a connection and relationship this is! And if such relationships, such spiritual influences and effects are found among the various members of the body of man, which is only one particular being among many, then there must assuredly exist both spiritual and material relationships among the countless universal beings.

order.why: Hear the reported relation between a physical voice and an inward effect.
Read the reported influence of air, scenery, fragrance and music.
Keep the reported distinction between divine and earthly music.
Read the reported image of deeds painting within human hearts.
shortened: Upon the canvas of creation with the brush of their deeds and [lives] and actions, they paint immortal pictures which cannot be found in any Art Museum of Europe and America but you find these masterpieces of these spiritual Artists in the hearts.

order.why: Reflect on pages valued through their connection with meaning.
shortened: Although the pages of a book know nothing of the words and the meanings traced upon them, even so, because of their connection with these words, friends pass them reverently from hand to hand. This connection, furthermore, is purest bounty.

order.why: Consider the reported spiritual effect of constructing a House of Worship.
Read the reported image of the Temple quickening a spiritual body.
shortened: Know ye that when this Temple of God shall be built in Chicago it will be to the spiritual body of the world what the inrush of the spirit is to the physical body of man, quickening it to its utmost parts and infusing a New Light and Power.

order.why: Keep the historical report concerning reverence toward places associated with apostles.
Examine the reported correspondence of the material and spiritual worlds.
Read scientific and religious understanding through the Tablet’s image of correspondence.
shortened: You have asked how we can harmonize scientific theories ["philosophical ideas"; afkar-i-faylasufi] with the ideas of religion [afkar-i-diyanati]. Know that this material world is the mirror of the Kingdom, and each of these worlds is in complete correspondence with the other. The correct theories of this world which are the result of sound scientific thinking are in agreement with the divine verses without the slightest divergence between them, for the truth of all things is laid away in the treasuries of the Kingdom.

order.why: Hear the reported chain from outward appearances to inner realities.
Consider the signs by which an unseen human spiritual world is known.
Read the reported correction of an inference of asceticism.
Join material conditions with the need for spiritual virtues.
shortened: The limited is ever in need of the unlimited. The material must be correlated with the spiritual. The material may be likened to the body, but divine virtues are the breathings of the Holy Spirit itself.

order.why: Distinguish the reported needs of body and spirit.
Read the reported account of participation in nature and the gift of spirit.
shortened: In brief, I have explained every proof and made clear every evidence that in the human world there is a spiritual power, there is an active spirit, and by this man is distinguished from that which is below man. Man shares with all beings in all degrees, but through the gift of spirit he is distinguished from all creation. This spirit is a breath of the divine breaths and a ray from the Sun of Reality.

order.why: Consider the reported life of the soul through its effects in humanity.
shortened: But the life of the soul is life. It is a life whereby the human world is illumined, and which distinguishes man from the animal. It is a life which is imperishable and everlasting; it is the very radiance of the grace of God. The spiritual life of man is the cause of attaining eternal glory; the spiritual life of man is the cause of drawing near to God; the spiritual life of man is the cause of gaining admittance into the Kingdom of God; the spiritual life of man is the cause of obtaining universal virtues; the spiritual life of man is the cause of shedding illumination upon the world of humanity.

order.why: Keep the reported analogy of spirit and bodily movement.
Read the reported interaction of bodily illness and mind without treating it as medical instruction.
Consider the letter’s account of physical and spiritual relations in its own terms.
Hear the reported explanation of spiritual emotion affecting nerves and body.
shortened: 'Abdu'l-Baha: "No it is not a physical condition, but spiritual, a very high one which is so intense it reaches the nerves and these react upon the body. When one is spiritually developed, the body responds to spiritual conditions or emotions."

order.why: Preserve the source’s incomplete reported statement about bodily improvement.
Read the reported location of happiness in the heart.
shortened: Man's happiness has its source in the heart, not in the body. When his heart is glad, a man is happy, though in prison. When his heart is sad, he can not be happy, though in a paradise.

order.why: Distinguish complementary political and spiritual orders.
shortened: There are two kinds of order, temporal and spiritual; political and divine - and both are necessary and complementary. The political order illumines the world, while the divine order transforms hearts into a rose garden. The former maintains control and discipline over bodies, while the latter serves to protect, preserve and quicken spirits.

order.why: Keep the historical East–West comparison in its public-address setting.
Turn the reported call for material reform toward spiritual reform.
shortened: If these material tendencies are in such need of reformation, how much greater the need in the world of the human spirit, the world of human thought, perception, virtues and bounties!

order.why: Read the reported image of Earth as a workshop of character.
shortened: Yet man must ever remember the earth plane is a workshop, not an art gallery for the exhibits of powers. This is not the plane of perfection, but earth is the crucible for refining and moulding character.

order.why: Consider the invitation to connect the material and divine realms.
shortened: You will establish a connection between the divine realm and the material world, and become an intermediary between the realm of place and placelessness.

order.why: Connects spiritual teaching with material institutions of education and charitable care.
Read the image of a wire connecting separated realms.
shortened: Now, this nearness is not confined to earthly regions - rather, the possible has drawn near to the impossible, the lowest center has drawn close to the Supreme Concourse, and connections have been established between the world of dust and the sacred realm. One end of the wire is fixed at the center of transmission and the other end in the Kingdom of the All-Forgiving Lord.

order.why: Keep the letter’s imagery of inner and outer worlds stirred together.
Distinguish relative measures of time from the divine realm.
Hear the reported dependence of solar time on sunrise and sunset.
shortened: Time with us is measured by the sun. When there is no more sunrise, and no more sunset, that kind of time does not exist for man.

order.why: Examine the question of a link beyond bodily existence.
shortened: Moreover you have asked about the link [barzakh] between the material world and the spiritual world. You have stated that since there was a link between the mineral and the vegetable kingdoms and one between the vegetable and animal kingdoms, such a link may also exist between the material and the spiritual worlds after ascension. Know thou of a certainty that the soul is exalted above time and place and that the intervening link is also spiritual by nature, wholly detached from the contingent world.

order.why: Consider the contrast between narrow dust and a radiant world.
Read the reported relation between degrees of existence.
Keep the reported description of sight in the spiritual world.
Consider the reported perception of earthly events through their spiritual effects.
shortened: To this he replied: "They see all as it affects the spirit. A great joy, a great sorrow, a sin, or a good deed: as these things darken or cloud the soul, or cause it to rise into greater light, so they see every earth event that touches you for good or ill, reflected in your soul.

order.why: Hear the reported claim of interaction across worlds.
shortened: There is no doubt that the forces of the higher worlds interplay with the forces of this plane. The heart of man is open to inspiration; this is spiritual communication.

order.why: Read the reported continuing relation with those beyond this life.
Consider the reported unveiling of gifts and limitations after death.
shortened: Just in the same way, while in this material world those who know God do not realise the blessings which He has conferred upon them; nor do those who know Him not realise the deficiencies of their state, when they leave the world of men for the spiritual realms, the gifts which God has bestowed upon them will be revealed to those who attain to Him; while the imperfections of those who walk in darkness, whose sight is veiled from God and who are bound down by attachment, will become plain to them also.

order.why: Keep the reported interpretation of Christ’s bodily sorrow.
shortened: I said: The answer to your question is very simple and given in a few words: The body or the flesh was 'sorrowful and very heavy' (Math chap 26th v. 37) because it loathed to be separated from the companionship of such a divine, celestial Spirit and be returned to clay and dust.

order.why: Turn to bonds of the heart when correspondence is prevented.
Read spiritual nearness across physical distance.
Consider present affection and hoped-for companionship in the Kingdom.
shortened: Though we are in the Holy Land and you are in the continent of America, yet the heart connections are firm and strong, for divine oneness has connected us, and in this physical world we are linked with one another, and God willing in the divine world, the realm of the Kingdom, we shall become intimate companions and confidants.

order.why: Read friendship in relation to an eternal world.
shortened: O thou who art firm in the Covenant! In this corporeal world, despite the separation of bodies, friends remain friends and intimate with each other. In the eternal world, then, which is the world of divine unity and heavenly oneness, friendship and spiritual intimacy are naturally among the essential requisites of that sanctified world....

order.why: Consider love’s freedom from physical nearness.
Keep the uncertain translated wording concerning spiritual fellowship.
Read the reported distinction of two worlds in an inquiry into dissension.
shortened: But beyond this, I want to use the opportunity presented to us by your question, in order to say something to you about the most profound cause of all dissensions:

Do not all the Prophets teach: there are two worlds, a spiritual one - the Malakut-i-Allah - the realm of God - and a material world, the world of nature in the widest meaning. Well, in the physical world, in the realm of the material, the battle for existence - the struggle for a more-or-less bare subsistence - is the dominating undertone of everything.

order.why: Close the linked passages with the reported continuity of service across life and death.
Preserve the supplied image of the body as the throne of the inner temple.
Compare the supplied Plotinian fragment while keeping its omissions visible.
Read the supplied application of bodily reciprocity to community life.
Close with the supplied account of mutual influence between inner life and environment.

questions: What does the example of music reveal about the relationship between sensation, feeling, and spiritual life?
How can an environment both express inward values and help cultivate them?
Which distinctions are needed when a passage moves from an analogy to a claim about unseen relationships?
How do the selections hold bodily needs together with a life of the spirit?
What does Aristotle’s concern with music and character add to this discussion, and where does its scope differ?
How might a community’s art, places of worship, and everyday surroundings support the qualities it wishes to develop?

references.label: 1 · Aristotle, Politics VIII.5 · Music, feeling, and character
references.note: In Benjamin Jowett’s translation, Aristotle asks whether music serves relaxation, cultivated enjoyment, or education. He argues that rhythm and melody affect feelings and can help form character. Compare this with the compilation’s examples of sound influencing the spirit. His civic educational argument, including its ancient social assumptions, is distinct from the Bahá’í account of spiritual life and does not establish the wider claims about relations between worlds.

subjects.displayTitle: Excellence: giving one’s best in service
subjects.introduction: Whoever has a craft, Bahá’u’lláh said, must carry it to perfection, even if the craft is weaving coarse straw mats; and joy is promised to the craftsman who perfects his work and deals fairly with everyone. Excellence in the Bahá’í writings begins that low to the ground and that close to justice. It is a distinction, but not the kind the world usually counts. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá told His listeners that He desired distinction for them, and then refused wealth, commerce, even science as its measure: the distinction He wanted was in morals, in character, in benefit to others. Honour lies in wisdom and praiseworthy conduct, not in riches, ancestry or fine clothes. The demand is nonetheless exacting. Students are told to stand at the head of the class by hard study and true merit, teachers to struggle unceasingly to perfect themselves, builders to finish an edifice with grace, villagers to shun slothfulness. Aristotle, who held that we become builders by building and just by doing just acts, explains why the quality of practice matters so much [1]: how we work forms who we become. The road passes through the education of children, self-improvement and discipline, and the virtuous life the spiritual path requires.
subjects.arc: Begin with the dignity of ordinary craft, define worthy distinction, and follow disciplined learning into work that benefits others.

order.why: Make social good a measure of individual distinction.
Open with the reported dignity of perfecting even coarse straw matting.
Join accomplished craft with equitable treatment of people.
Distinguish honor from accumulated wealth and vainglory.
shortened: Man's honor lieth in wisdom, understanding and praiseworthy character, not in the accumulation of riches and pride and vainglory.

order.why: Read the public address’s emphasis on moral distinction.
shortened: I desire distinction for you. The Baha'is must be distinguished from others of humanity. But this distinction must not depend upon wealth -- that they should become more affluent than other people. I do not desire for you financial distinction. It is not an ordinary distinction I desire; not scientific, commercial, industrial distinction. For you I desire spiritual distinction -- that is, you must become eminent and distinguished in morals.

order.why: Keep the parallel reported formulation of spiritual distinction.
shortened: But this distinction must not depend upon wealth - that they should become more affluent than other people. I do not desire for you financial distinction. It is not an ordinary distinction that I desire; not scientific, commercial, industrial distinction.
For you I desire spiritual distinction; that is, you must become eminent and distinguished in morals.

order.why: Set knowledge and refinement beside inherited status.
Consider recognition beyond outward strength and riches.
shortened: O handmaiden! Today there are many strong ones, mighty ones and wealthy ones on earth who are deprived due to heedlessness, while you are mentioned in the presence.

order.why: Read the influence of those without prior fame.
shortened: But those weak souls who outwardly had neither fame nor sign, because they entered beneath the shadow of the Divine Word, their signs and lights became manifest throughout all the divine realms, even present in the very dust of the earth.

order.why: Introduce perfection as each thing’s paradise.
Read the Báb’s demanding injunction concerning craftsmanship.
shortened: Therefore in every Revelation, the inhabitants of the previous Revelation are rendered as naught. O thou manifestation of perfection, perfect all thy craft and craftsmanship, and learn from that concerning the letters of the Gospel, such that thou mayest write from the Most Exalted Point what is possible therein of craftsmanship. I have given thee the part as an example that thou mayest know the whole from the part. Verily God hath cursed one who is capable of manifesting a craft in perfection yet manifests it imperfectly, and who loves for himself what he would purchase from another.

order.why: Balance perfect penmanship with the use of time for beneficial sciences.
shortened: Although for some, sufficient penmanship to meet their needs may suffice - and it would be better and more fitting to spend time in beneficial sciences - yet since God, exalted be His glory, hath loved every craft at its most perfect, therefore that which flowed from the Most Exalted Pen was revealed.

order.why: Consider concentration on a craft as a condition of proficiency.
Read the reported value of specialization in its watchmaking context.
Join thoroughness of faith with proficiency in medicine and surgery.
shortened: O my loved one! Thoroughness in every undertaking is among the fruits of faith and certitude. Therefore strive to become truly proficient in medicine and surgery to the extent possible, and this is what is hoped for if the aforementioned praiseworthy Prince agrees to it in keeping with the kindness he has shown you.

order.why: Keep spiritual guidance beside the letter’s concern with healing.
shortened: For guidance is the medicine of the spirit and the cause of spiritual victories - it is healing for the soul and a remedy of joy and delight for the heart.

order.why: Read perfection in a profession as worship.
Consider the value of accomplished work at the divine threshold.
Follow the invitation to pursue trained abilities to their limit.
Link gratitude with daily progress in a craft.
Keep the call for unceasing personal improvement.
shortened: You must, however, struggle unceasingly to perfect yourself and win ever higher achievements.

order.why: Consider the warning about unfinished endeavors.
shortened: In affairs one must achieve complete perfection, otherwise no result is yielded and no fruit obtained; rather it remains incomplete.

order.why: Hear the reported influence of devotion to a vocation.
Read the reported expression of divine qualities through work.
shortened: Man must work and in that work show the qualities of GOD and thus do good. His work, both material and spiritual, must show what he is. By his arts, sciences, inventions and all of his work he must show his best ability.

order.why: Join artistic development and spiritual service.
shortened: Therefore, extreme effort should be made in art and this will not prevent the teaching of the people in that region. Nay, rather, each should assist the other in art and guidance. For instance, when the studying of art is with the intention of obeying the command (of God) this study will certainly be done easily and great progress will soon be made therein; and when others discover this fragrance of spirituality in the action itself, this same will cause their awakening.

order.why: Read the tailor’s work as a metaphor for adorning collective life.
Consider encouragement offered to a poet.
Read proficiency in language alongside cooperative service.
Connect learning with the capacity for fluent public speech.
shortened: When this is achieved, you will become zealous and courageous in acquiring sciences and arts, and will speak English with perfect eloquence and fluency, even delivering eloquent and fluent speeches in public gatherings.

order.why: Keep the reported musician’s development in its biographical setting.
shortened: In a short while he became famous throughout all Bagdad and leaving his hard labor of thorn-picking he devoted his career to the inspiring art of music. With his growing popularity he grew in wealth and position and became a respected, loved and honored member of the community.

order.why: Read the reported counsel about virtue within theatrical life.
shortened: Strive for that which prompts the personification of dignity and virtues. The theatrical world need not prevent your development.

order.why: Join academic learning with the school of inner meanings.
shortened: It is the longing desire of Abdu'l-Baha to see each one of you accounted as the foremost professor in the academies, and in the school of inner significances, each one becoming a leader in wisdom.

order.why: Hear the reported invitation to enlarge ideals and endeavors.
shortened: Exalt your thoughts. Reflect over all your affairs. Magnify your endeavors. Enlarge the circle of your ideals. Open the wings of spiritual wisdom. Let your hope be the accomplishment of most great deeds the results of which may immortalize your names.

order.why: Read the demanding reported exhortation to college students.
shortened: I hope that while you are studying in this college you may so excel all other students in the various branches of Knowledge taught therein;- that all of them may testify that these Baha'i students have another power, they are inspired with another effort, they are imbued with a nobler ambition and they are stimulated by higher motives and wider and deeper exertion. Were you to be equal with them, then what distinction will there remain for you; therefore you must strive to be superior to them so that every one may bear testimony to this fact.

order.why: Keep the particular call to distinguish oneself in Beirut studies.
shortened: In the college and schools of Beirut, you must all exert such intense effort and decisive endeavor in your studies that you may distinguish yourselves among all the students.

order.why: Consider the reported emphasis on hard study and true merit.
shortened: Strive always to be at the head of your class through hard study and true merit...

order.why: Read the reported classroom use of questions and encouragement.
Consider the aim that each child flourish.
shortened: When matters are thus well arranged, every child will become a peerless plant in the gardens of the Abha Paradise.

order.why: Keep the aspiration for a school’s excellence and graduates.
Read the reported ideal of sympathetic and refined teachers.
shortened: The teachers and professors will be spiritual and their idealism sublime and transcendent. Their sympathetic and artistic natures will be acute and most refined.

order.why: Connect the acquisition of knowledge with service to Iran.
Consider the reported choice of disciplines that contribute to national revival.
Join public duties with justice and trustworthiness.
Read particular counsel about conduct in government employment.
Hear the reported distinction based on service rather than a father’s rank.
Read skill and zeal in a proposed commercial partnership.
Consider proficiency and steadfastness in company establishments.
Read care and refinement in a building undertaking.
Keep the further counsel to complete an edifice diligently.
shortened: But you must complete the blessed undertaking of the established edifice with utmost diligence, in perfect grace and elegance.

order.why: Hear the reported call to diligent work addressed to villagers.
shortened: Co-operate with each other and be always quick to learn. Shun slothfulness. Be diligent in your work.

order.why: Consider the reported encouragement to work patiently for results.
Keep the historical report about Greek enterprise in its particular voice.
Retain the reported youthful feat as an anecdote about skill.
Read the reported enjoyment of becoming more accomplished and upright.
shortened: Truly they have borne themselves with urbanity and dignity. May they ever become better, sweeter, more perfect and more accomplished! In this path lies lifeis enjoyment. The success and pleasure of this physical life lies in uprightness!

order.why: Consider an enduring name associated with wisdom and kindness.
Read the collective aspiration to surpass earlier conduct in spiritual qualities.
Bring excellence together with purity, health, knowledge and self-control.
Close with the invitation to manifest sincerity within one’s own capacity.
Distinguishes degrees of excellence in obligatory and voluntary deeds.

questions: What makes excellence in a humble craft spiritually significant?
How do these passages distinguish worthy ambition from pride in wealth, ancestry, or reputation?
How can encouragement and high expectations help each learner flourish without reducing worth to rank?
What do concentration, repeated practice, and cooperation each contribute to proficiency?
How does Aristotle’s account of habit illuminate the connection between the quality of work and the formation of character?
What would become different in your own work if benefit to others helped define success?

references.label: 1 · Aristotle, Nicomachean Ethics II.1 · Becoming through practice
references.note: In W. D. Ross’s translation, Aristotle compares acquiring virtue with learning a craft: repeated actions form capacities and habits, for better or worse. Practice therefore requires attention to its quality. Compare this with the compilation’s invitations to proficiency, truthful conduct, and sustained effort. Aristotle’s account of habituation offers a practical point of contact while the Bahá’í passages also frame work as worship and service to a divine purpose.

subjects.displayTitle: Parents and children: care, gratitude, and growing responsibility
subjects.introduction: Asked once what His faith taught about the family, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá answered with a catalogue of rights: the son’s, the father’s, the mother’s, the sister’s, none to be transgressed and none arbitrary, the injury of one counted the injury of all. Everything else about parents and children rests on that mutuality. A home without children is a home without light; parents learn that their example teaches what instruction cannot, and that regard for parents stands next after the oneness of God itself. The Qur’án joins gratitude to parents with worship of the One, yet adds that a parent demanding idolatry is not to be obeyed, though still kept company with courteously, and that pairing of gratitude with conscience keeps this subject from becoming a charter for mere obedience [1]. The road leads on into the education of children, into prayer for parents who may not share one’s faith, and into inheritance and the rights of the eldest son through which one generation hands its trust to the next.
subjects.arc: Begin with mutual rights and affection, consider education and filial responsibility, and follow growing capacities into the service of the wider community.

order.why: Open with the rights and obligations of every member of the family.
shortened: The integrity of the family bond must be constantly considered, and the rights of the individual members must not be transgressed. The rights of the son, the father, the mother -- none of them must be transgressed, none of them must be arbitrary. Just as the son has certain obligations to his father, the father, likewise, has certain obligations to his son. The mother, the sister and other members of the household have their certain prerogatives. All these rights and prerogatives must be conserved, yet the unity of the family must be sustained. The injury of one shall be considered the injury of all; the comfort of each, the comfort of all; the honor of one, the honor of all.

order.why: Hear the reported memory of a child’s affectionate embrace.
shortened: I had a son about three or four years old. This child was a great comfort to me. Often, past midnight while I was sound sleep, the child would leave his small bed and slowly creep in toward mine and putting his lovely little arms around my neck and kiss my closed eyelids and face. Then I would wake and endear and love it. That state-that happiness-that beatific joy - that is to wake up and find your beloved child clasping his tiny arms around your neck - is only known to a father.

order.why: Read the reciprocal joy of loving parents and a worthy child.
Consider the letter requested by a father remembering his child.
shortened: O thou servant of Baha!

Thy father is present in this gathering and requested this letter. Consider how dear is a father who, in this gathering, is intimately engaged in remembrance of thee and familiar with thy mention, and who begs from God that thou mayest be confirmed. At every moment thou shouldst offer a hundred thousand thanks that thou hast such a loving father and art confirmed in the grace and bounty of the Ancient Beauty.

order.why: Read the joy of children becoming spiritual lights.
Consider the reported ideal of a joyful and harmonious home.
shortened: In this glorious Cause the life of a married couple should resemble the life of the angels in heaven -- a life full of joy and spiritual delight, a life of unity and concord, a friendship both mental and physical.

Even as two birds they should warble melodies upon the branches of the tree of fellowship and harmony. They should always be elated with joy and gladness and be a source of happiness to the hearts of others. They should set an example to their fellow-men, manifest a true and sincere love towards each other and educate their children in such a manner as to blazon the fame and glory of their family.

order.why: Keep the reported image of children as light in a home.
Place parental example before instruction alone.
Hear the reported shared responsibility of father and mother.
Establish the duty to educate both sons and daughters.
Consider the mother’s own learning and accomplishments.
Read the emphasis on early formation and the difficulty of changing habits.
shortened: Education and refinement after maturity becomes extremely difficult. Experience has shown that despite utmost effort to change even one trait in someone's character, it proves impossible. If today they become somewhat aware, after a few days they forget and return to their habitual state and accustomed ways.

order.why: Give the education of a son an aim in love and harmony.
Consider the reported relation between encouragement and noble qualities.
shortened: When the child sees that the parents love him more for his good qualities than purely for his own self, then he will endeavor to obey his parents by characterizing himself with noble qualities. For he will know that by this means, his parents' love for him will increase, and that to neglect this, he shall forfeit their greater love and affection.

order.why: Read the parents’ responsibility for religious formation.
Link regard for parents with recognition of divine unity.
shortened: The fruits of the tree of existence are trustworthiness, religion, truthfulness and sincerity, and greatest of all, after the oneness of God, exalted and mighty be He, is due regard for the rights of parents.

Consider what the All-Merciful has revealed in the Qur'an, His words exalted be He: "Worship God and associate naught with Him, and show kindness unto parents." Observe how kindness to parents is joined with the oneness of God.

order.why: Keep the parallel Tablet’s scriptural appeal to parental rights.
shortened: And the greatest of all, after recognition of the unity of the Lord, exalted and glorified be He, is regard for the rights of one's parents. This matter hath been mentioned in all the heavenly Books and recorded by the Most Exalted Pen. Consider what the All-Merciful hath revealed in the Qur'an: "Worship God and join not any partners with Him, and show kindness unto parents." Observe how association with parents is linked with the recognition of the one true God.

order.why: Read the concise linking of parental and divine rights.
shortened: These are the parents of whom He says: "Worship God and associate naught with Him, and show kindness unto parents." He hath joined their rights with the rights of His Divinity.

order.why: Consider maturity for religious duties beside regard for parents.
shortened: 20. QUESTION:  Concerning the age of maturity with respect to religious duties.
ANSWER:  The age of maturity is fifteen for both men and women.

The fruits that best befit the tree of human life are trustworthiness and godliness, truthfulness and sincerity; but greater than all, after recognition of the unity of God, praised and glorified be He, is regard for the rights that are due to one's parents.  This teaching hath been mentioned in all the Books of God, and reaffirmed by the Most Exalted Pen.  Consider that which the Merciful Lord hath revealed in the Qur'an, exalted are His words:  "Worship ye God, join with Him no peer or likeness; and show forth kindliness and charity towards your parents..."  Observe how loving-kindness to one's parents hath been linked to recognition of the one true God!

order.why: Read service to parents as a path of service to God.
shortened: Beware lest ye commit that which would sadden the hearts of your fathers and mothers. Follow ye the path of Truth, which indeed is a straight path. Should anyone give you a choice between the opportunity to render a service to Me and a service to them, choose ye to serve them, and let such service be a path leading you to Me.

order.why: Establish the qualification concerning nearness to the divine threshold.
Read patience toward a parent beside the letter’s phrase about what is possible.
shortened: Seek the good pleasure of thy father as far as it is possible for thee and be not aggrieved by his indifference for the rights of one's parents are sacred even should they perpetrate injustices against thee.

order.why: Keep counsel concerning patience with a father in its particular setting.
Preserve the individual letter’s emphatic counsel to seek paternal good pleasure.
shortened: Convey yearning greetings to your esteemed father, act according to his good pleasure, and carry out whatever he deems advisable. Set aside your own thoughts and execute whatever is his will. Do not deviate from his good pleasure by so much as a hair's breadth, and know that this is the cause of your eternal happiness.

order.why: Read the son’s duty of attention to a father’s comfort.
shortened: The son, on the other hand, must show forth the utmost obedience towards his father, and should conduct himself as a humble and a lowly servant. Day and night he should seek diligently to ensure the comfort and welfare of his loving father and to secure his good pleasure.

order.why: Consider the sacred weight assigned to filial duties.
shortened: There are also certain sacred duties on children toward parents, which duties are written in the Book of God, as belonging to God. The (children's) prosperity in this world and the Kingdom depends upon the good pleasure of parents, and without this they will be in manifest loss.

order.why: Join consideration for a mother with consideration for a brother.
