shortened: Know thou that the rights of parents are great, very great, and God hath compared them to His own rights. Thou must, therefore, please thy mother, obey her orders, and show consideration towards thy brother under all conditions, as required in the law of God.

order.why: Read affection and obedience within the recipient’s relationship to a father.
shortened: Satisfy thy revered father and seek his pleasure, so that he may consider that thou observest his obedience more than ever. Practice the utmost love and affection.

order.why: Keep the qualification of legitimacy in a letter about marriage and a mother’s wishes.
shortened: And if you wish to take a spouse in obedience to your mother, there is no objection to this, for mothers have rights conjoined with the rights of the Lord of verses. He has said in the Qur'an: "Lower unto them the wing of humility and say: My Lord! Have mercy on them even as they cherished me when I was little." Based on this, obeying one's mother in a legitimate matter is a gift to man.

order.why: Extend care for parents toward stranger and kin.
shortened: A son should be thus affectionate and worship his parents, forsake his own comfort and think of the ease of both stranger and kin.

order.why: Read gratitude for a child’s service to a mother.
Explains the formative influence of educating a child’s character.
Hear the reported encouragement addressed directly to children.
shortened: You must obey your parents so that they may be pleased with you, and so that God will be pleased with you, and that you may become the children of the Kingdom and mirror forth the words of Christ.

order.why: Consider the hope that youth combine service to faith and to a parent.
shortened: I send boundless greetings to thy honored son. I hope that through divine grace and favor he may be assisted and confirmed in his youth to serve the Cause and to serve thee, for the rights of parents are most great in the sight of the Beloved, especially in this matter wherein they have placed great emphasis.

order.why: Read the image of a new branch carrying forward a root’s life.
shortened: Thou art a memorial of that Tree of God's love; thou art a remnant of that sign of divine bounty. I beseech the Lord of existence, by His kindness and generosity, to reveal the truth of the saying "the child is the secret essence of its sire" in the inner reality of that new flower of the garden of recognition. Thus mayest the branch follow the way of the root "and that is not difficult for God."

order.why: Consider the special opportunity for steadfast service in youth.
shortened: He said: "Blessed is the one who arises to serve the Cause of the Lord of the beginning and the end in the prime of youth, and is adorned with His love. The appearance of this greatest bounty is greater than the creation of the heavens and earth. Blessed are the firm ones and joy be to the steadfast."

order.why: Read youth as a springtime of vigor, learning and unclouded motives.
Hear the public address’s account of capacities moving beyond childhood.
Consider divine loving-kindness toward parents beyond shared belief.
shortened: One of the special bounties vouchsafed in this Revelation is this: that every soul who turneth in faith toward the Dawning-Place of the Cause---his parents, albeit they have not attained unto faith in this Manifestation---shall yet be encompassed by the rays of the Sun of Divine loving-kindness, and shall be taken into its shelter. This is of His grace unto His loved ones. Render thou thanks, and be thou of the thankful.

order.why: Close the linked passages with the reported promise concerning parents.
Place the supplied counsel on loving consultation before further institutional guidance.
shortened: Baha'u'llah came to bring unity to the world, and a fundamental unity is that of the family. Therefore, one must believe that the Faith is intended to strengthen the family, not weaken it, and one of the keys to the strengthening of unity is loving consultation. The atmosphere within a Baha'i family as within the community as a whole should express 'the keynote of the Cause of God' which, the beloved Guardian has stated, 'is not dictatorial authority but humble fellowship, not arbitrary power, but the spirit of frank and loving consultation'.

order.why: Attend to the particular needs and capacities of junior youth.
Read children’s classes and youth participation within community building.
Join preparation for teaching with science, literature and the example of public speech.
Read the supplied call for intellectual and spiritual equipment.
Consider historical examples of service before later maturity.
Make selfless service central to the hopes placed in youth.
Read youthful adaptability and energy in relation to particular projects.
Consider participation across race, nationality and class.
shortened: No greater demonstration can be given to the peoples of both continents of the youthful vitality and the vibrant power animating the life, and the institutions of the nascent Faith of Baha'u'llah than an intelligent, persistent, and effective participation of the Baha'i youth, of every race, nationality, and class, in both the teaching and administrative spheres of Baha'i activity.

order.why: Keep the historical hopes for youth in teaching and administration.
Read the dated call to seize opportunities during a particular plan.
Keep the dated guidance on institutes and clusters in its historical setting.
Consider the supplied call to sympathize with peers amid social upheaval.
shortened: Even though the Baha'i Youth should feel with the condition in which they see their non-Baha'i friends and not indict them for it, they should not let themselves be carried by the wave of world events as they are being carried. Whereas they see before them only a world that is crumbling down we are also seeing a new world being built up. Whereas they experience the destruction of old institutions that commanded their respect, we are beholding the dawn of a new era with its strict commands and new social bonds. Their materialistic outlook shows them the futility of all things while our faith in a regenerated and spiritualized man makes us look to the future and build for it. To make them follow our ways we should sympathize with their plight but should not follow their ways. We should take our stand on a higher plane of moral and spiritual life and, setting for them the true example, urge them up to our level.

order.why: Read courage and justice as responses to wounded societies.
shortened: Be not dismayed if your endeavors are dismissed as utopian by the voices that would oppose any suggestion of fundamental change. Trust in the capacity of this generation to disentangle itself from the embroilments of a divided society. To discharge your responsibilities, you will have to show forth courage, the courage of those who cling to standards of rectitude, whose lives are characterized by purity of thought and action, and whose purpose is directed by love and indomitable faith. As you dedicate yourselves to healing the wounds with which your peoples have been afflicted, you will become invincible champions of justice.

order.why: Close with the supplied promise of mercy to kin and its stated qualification.

questions: How do mutual rights change the way the passages on family unity and obedience are read?
What does a parent’s example teach that instruction alone may not convey?
How can gratitude and care continue when parents and children differ in religious conviction?
What capacities and responsibilities change as a child enters junior youth and youth?
What does the Qur’anic pairing of non-obedience in religion with courteous companionship contribute to this discussion?
How might loving consultation help a family support both its members’ needs and their service to the wider world?

references.label: 1 · Qur’an 31:14–15 · Gratitude, conscience, and companionship
references.note: These verses join gratitude toward God and parents, recalling the mother’s hardships, with a limit: pressure to associate partners with God is not to be obeyed. Courteous companionship is still enjoined. Compare this combination with the compilation’s honor for parents and qualification concerning spiritual allegiance. The verses address a particular religious conflict; they do not by themselves settle every question about family authority or differing beliefs.
